# FINOS CCC-aligned private AKS cluster

This example deploys the AVM AKS resource module (`source = "../.."`) configured against the
[FINOS Common Cloud Controls (CCC) Kubernetes catalog](https://github.com/finos/common-cloud-controls/blob/443b0a2b27e2d9bdfe0abb2eb65a1865e5dbe416/catalogs/orchestration/k8s/controls.yaml)
and the CCC Core controls it imports. Every supporting resource uses a published Azure Verified
Module where one exists. Each Terraform block is annotated with the CCC assessment
requirements (ARs) it enforces.

> **Not an attestation.** The table below records which configuration enforces each AR. It is not an official CCC assessment, and live requirement results still need testing in the deployed environment.

## What it deploys

| Purpose | Module | CCC |
| --- | --- | --- |
| AKS cluster, managed namespaces and maintenance windows | this module (`../..`) | all |
| Resource group | `Azure/avm-res-resources-resourcegroup/azurerm` | Core.CN06 |
| Cluster and runner VNets, subnets | `Azure/avm-res-network-virtualnetwork/azurerm` | CN01, Core.CN05 |
| One NSG per subnet | `Azure/avm-res-network-networksecuritygroup/azurerm` | CN01, Core.CN05 |
| Control-plane, kubelet and workload identities | `Azure/avm-res-managedidentity-userassignedidentity/azurerm` | CN03, CN17 |
| API server, vault and registry private DNS | `Azure/avm-res-network-privatednszone/azurerm` | CN01 |
| Private Key Vault, KMS key and disk key | `Azure/avm-res-keyvault-vault/azurerm` (+ `//modules/key`) | CN07, Core.CN02 |
| Runner vault private endpoint | `Azure/avm-res-network-privateendpoint/azurerm` | CN07 |
| Disk encryption set | `Azure/avm-res-compute-diskencryptionset/azurerm` | Core.CN02 |
| Least-privilege infrastructure grants | `Azure/avm-res-authorization-roleassignment/azurerm` | CN17 |
| Private approved registry | `Azure/avm-res-containerregistry-registry/azurerm` | CN04 |
| Azure Policy for Kubernetes assignments | `Azure/avm-ptn-policyassignment/azurerm` | CN04, CN05, CN11, CN13 |
| Log Analytics workspace | `Azure/avm-res-operationalinsights-workspace/azurerm` | CN14, Core.CN04 |
| Activity log alert | `Azure/avm-res-insights-activitylogalert/azurerm` | CN14, CN11, CN15 |
| Kubernetes audit log alert | `azapi_resource` (`avm-res-insights-scheduledqueryrule` is only Proposed) | CN14 |

## CCC control mapping

Legend: **TF** enforced by Terraform-managed Azure configuration, **Policy** enforced at
admission by Azure Policy for Kubernetes, **K8s** enforced by Kubernetes objects created by the
example, **Residual** requires an operational process or is a platform limitation.

| AR | Enforcement | How |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CN01.AR01 | TF | Private cluster with API-server VNet integration; NSGs on every subnet. |
| CN01.AR02 | TF | `public_network_access = "Disabled"`, no public FQDN, Run Command disabled. |
| CN02.AR01 | TF | Entra ID with Azure RBAC for Kubernetes; scoped `cluster_role_assignments`; admin groups only for break-glass. |
| CN02.AR02 | Residual | Only built-in AKS RBAC roles are granted. Workload `Role` definitions belong to application teams and need review in CI. |
| CN03.AR01 | TF | OIDC issuer, workload identity and one federated identity per workload namespace service account. |
| CN03.AR02 | Residual | Scan manifests, Secrets and ConfigMaps for static credentials in CI. |
| CN04.AR01 | Policy | Allowed images: the private registry only, pinned by `@sha256` digest. |
| CN04.AR02 | Residual | Sign images in the build pipeline. AKS Image Integrity is preview and audit-only, so it is not enabled. |
| CN04.AR03 | Residual | Defender for Containers reports vulnerabilities; gate releases on them in the pipeline. |
| CN05.AR01/AR02 | Policy | Kubernetes restricted pod security standard initiative in `Deny` mode, with no added capabilities allowed and `ALL` capabilities required to be dropped. |
| CN06.AR01 | K8s | Managed namespaces with `DenyAll` ingress and egress, enforced by Cilium. |
| CN06.AR02 | Residual | Application teams add explicit allow policies with stable selectors. |
| CN07.AR01 | TF | Private Key Vault KMS for Kubernetes secrets, CMK disk encryption, workload identity for delivery. |
| CN07.AR02 | Residual | Workload `Role` definitions must name the secrets they read. |
| CN08.AR01 | TF | `check "approved_addons_only"` compares the enabled add-ons with `var.approved_addons`. |
| CN09.AR01–AR03 | TF | Standard tier, `patch` and `NodeImage` upgrade channels, weekly maintenance windows, AKS-managed add-ons only. |
| CN10.AR01/AR02 | Residual | Storage-class and volume re-use policy are not configured by the example. |
| CN11.AR01 | Policy | Deny-mode assignments cover every non-system namespace; AKS manages system-namespace exclusions. |
| CN11.AR02 | TF | Policy changes need Azure policy permissions, are logged and raise the activity log alert. |
| CN11.AR03 | Residual | Gatekeeper webhook failure behavior is managed by the Azure Policy add-on. |
| CN12.AR01 | TF | AKS-managed kubelet authentication and authorization; anonymous access is disabled by the platform. |
| CN12.AR02 | TF | `ssh_access = "Disabled"`, no node public IPs. |
| CN12.AR03 | K8s | Default-deny egress blocks the instance metadata endpoint from workload namespaces. |
| CN13.AR01 | Policy | Every container must declare limits within `container_cpu_limit` and `container_memory_limit`. |
| CN13.AR02 | K8s | Namespace CPU and memory quotas. Storage and object-count quotas need an additional `ResourceQuota`. |
| CN13.AR03 | TF | Cluster autoscaler with an explicit `max_count`. |
| CN14.AR01 | TF | Diagnostic settings (all log groups), Container Insights and Defender to Log Analytics. |
| CN14.AR02 | TF | Separate workspace; no cluster, kubelet or workload identity is granted access to it. |
| CN14.AR03 | TF | Activity log alert for ARM changes and a KQL alert for Kubernetes RBAC, webhook and network policy changes. |
| CN15.AR01 | TF | Required `owner`, `environment` and `data-classification` tags; namespace labels and annotations. |
| CN15.AR02 | TF | Node resource group `ReadOnly` lockdown; metadata changes raise the activity log alert. |
| CN16.AR01/AR02 | TF | Managed Entra ID authentication; local accounts disabled. |
| CN17.AR01/AR02 | TF | Distinct control-plane, kubelet and workload identities; grants scoped to subnets, zone, identity and keys. |
| CN18.AR01/AR02 | TF | AKS-supplied Ubuntu images with Secure Boot and vTPM. |

## Prerequisites

- Permission to create resources and role assignments in the target subscription or resource group
  (for example Owner, or Contributor plus Role Based Access Control Administrator).
- The `Microsoft.Compute/EncryptionAtHost` feature registered on the subscription, and the
  `Microsoft.ContainerService`, `Microsoft.KeyVault`, `Microsoft.Network`, `Microsoft.ContainerRegistry`,
  `Microsoft.OperationalInsights`, `Microsoft.Insights` and `Microsoft.PolicyInsights` providers registered.
- A region that supports zones 1–3, Trusted Launch, encryption at host and `Standard_D4s_v5`.
- A Defender for Containers plan if Defender findings are required (CN04.AR03, CN14).

## Deploying

The Key Vault keys are created through the vault's private endpoint, so Terraform must run from a
host that can reach the runner VNet. This is the reason the example is excluded from automated E2E.

```powershell
terraform -chdir=examples/finos-ccc init
# 1. Create the resource group, VNets and NSGs.
terraform -chdir=examples/finos-ccc apply -target=module.virtual_networks
# 2. Place a self-hosted runner or jump host in the `runner_subnet_id` output (or connect to the
#    runner VNet through VPN or peering), then run the full deployment from there.
terraform -chdir=examples/finos-ccc apply
# 3. Check idempotency: exit code 0 means no changes.
terraform -chdir=examples/finos-ccc plan -detailed-exitcode
```

Without explicit `cluster_role_assignments`, the deploying identity receives
`Azure Kubernetes Service RBAC Cluster Admin`. Supply group-based, narrower roles for anything
beyond a demonstration. The API server is private and Run Command is disabled, so `kubectl` access
also requires a host in, or connected to, the cluster VNet.

## Reusing existing resources

Every prerequisite is created by default. Supply existing IDs to reuse them instead; nothing is
imported, and existing-to-existing role assignments stay with their owner.

| Input | Behavior when null |
| --- | --- |
| `resource_group_id` | Create a resource group. |
| `subnet_id`, `api_server_subnet_id`, `key_vault_private_endpoint_subnet_id`, `container_registry_private_endpoint_subnet_id` | Supply all four or none. When null, create the cluster and runner VNets. |
| `control_plane_identity_id`, `kubelet_identity_id` | Create distinct user-assigned identities. |
| `private_dns_zone_id` | Create `ccc-<suffix>.private.<location>.azmk8s.io` linked to the cluster VNet. |
| `key_vault_resource_id`, `key_vault_key_id` | Create a private, RBAC, purge-protected vault and an RSA-3072 KMS key. `key_vault_key_id` is a versioned HTTPS key URL. |
| `disk_encryption_set_id` | Create a separate disk key and a system-assigned DES. |
| `key_vault_private_dns_zone_id`, `container_registry_private_dns_zone_id` | Create the `privatelink` zones. Do not link the vault zone to the cluster VNet; AKS private KMS links its own. |

Grants are created only for a new principal or target. When the deployment creates the vault, the
deployer receives Key Vault Crypto Officer on that vault so it can create the keys. On a reused vault
the deployer must already hold that role, and the vault must use RBAC (and purge protection when a
DES is created).

## Key lifecycle

Legacy `azure_key_vault_kms` is used. Automatic key rotation and expiry are not configured; rotate
keys with the documented legacy KMS procedure. Destroy soft-deletes keys managed by this example
(including keys created in a reused vault). Purge-on-destroy is disabled, and a created vault is
retained under its 90-day purge protection. Never delete a key while a cluster still needs it.

```hcl
provider "azapi" {
  subscription_id = local.subscription_id
}

# Published prerequisite AVM modules require AzureRM; the AKS module itself uses AzAPI.
provider "azurerm" {
  subscription_id                 = local.subscription_id
  resource_provider_registrations = "none"

  features {
    key_vault {
      purge_soft_delete_on_destroy       = false
      purge_soft_deleted_keys_on_destroy = false
      recover_soft_deleted_key_vaults    = false
      recover_soft_deleted_keys          = false
    }
  }
}

resource "random_string" "name_suffix" {
  length  = 8
  special = false
  upper   = false
}

# Fresh role assignments can take minutes to propagate; AKS validates BYO identity
# permissions at create time.
resource "time_sleep" "rbac_propagation" {
  create_duration = "60s"

  depends_on = [module.prerequisite_role_assignments]
}

# Each attribute below is annotated with the FINOS CCC K8S assessment requirements (ARs)
# it enforces. See _header.md for the complete control matrix and residual items.
module "aks" {
  source = "../.."
  providers = {
    azapi = azapi
  }

  # CCC.Core.CN06: approved region.
  location  = var.location
  name      = local.cluster_name
  parent_id = local.resource_group_id
  # CCC.K8S.CN02.AR01 / CN16.AR01: Entra ID with Azure RBAC for Kubernetes authorization.
  # Admin groups are reserved for break-glass access.
  aad_profile = {
    managed                = true
    enable_azure_rbac      = true
    admin_group_object_ids = var.cluster_admin_group_object_ids
  }
  # CCC.K8S.CN04/CN05/CN11/CN13: the Azure Policy add-on enforces the assignments in
  # main.governance.tf. CCC.K8S.CN08.AR01: add-ons come from the allowlist check below.
  addon_profile_azure_policy = local.addon_profile_azure_policy
  # CCC.K8S.CN14.AR01: Container Insights with Entra ID authentication.
  addon_profile_oms_agent = {
    enabled = local.addon_profile_oms_agent_enabled
    config = {
      log_analytics_workspace_resource_id = module.log_analytics.resource_id
      use_aad_auth                        = true
    }
  }
  # CCC.K8S.CN01.AR01/AR02, CCC.Core.CN05: private API server reachable only from the
  # cluster VNet; no public FQDN and no Run Command.
  api_server_access_profile = {
    enable_private_cluster             = true
    enable_private_cluster_public_fqdn = false
    enable_vnet_integration            = true
    disable_run_command                = true
    private_dns_zone                   = local.private_dns_zone_id
    subnet_id                          = local.api_server_subnet_id
  }
  # CCC.K8S.CN09.AR01/AR02: managed patch and node-image upgrades.
  auto_upgrade_profile = {
    upgrade_channel         = "patch"
    node_os_upgrade_channel = "NodeImage"
  }
  # CCC.K8S.CN12.AR02: SSH disabled, no public node IPs.
  # CCC.K8S.CN18.AR01/AR02: AKS-supplied image with Secure Boot and vTPM (Trusted Launch).
  # CCC.Core.CN02: encryption at host in addition to the DES.
  # CCC.K8S.CN13.AR03: autoscaler with an explicit maximum.
  default_agent_pool = {
    name                      = "systempool"
    vm_size                   = "Standard_D4s_v5"
    count_of                  = 2
    min_count                 = 2
    max_count                 = 5
    max_pods                  = 30
    vnet_subnet_id            = local.node_subnet_id
    os_sku                    = "Ubuntu"
    os_disk_type              = "Managed"
    enable_auto_scaling       = true
    enable_encryption_at_host = true
    enable_node_public_ip     = false
    availability_zones        = ["1", "2", "3"]
    security_profile = {
      enable_secure_boot = true
      enable_vtpm        = true
      ssh_access         = "Disabled"
    }
  }
  # CCC.K8S.CN14.AR01 / CCC.Core.CN04: Kubernetes audit and control-plane logs to an
  # external Log Analytics workspace.
  diagnostic_settings = {
    log_analytics = {
      name                           = "ds-aks-ccc"
      workspace_resource_id          = module.log_analytics.resource_id
      log_analytics_destination_type = "Dedicated"
      log_groups                     = ["allLogs"]
    }
  }
  # CCC.K8S.CN16.AR02: no local accounts or static credentials.
  disable_local_accounts = true
  # CCC.Core.CN02 / CCC.K8S.CN07.AR01: customer-managed key for node disks.
  disk_encryption_set_id = local.disk_encryption_set_id
  enable_rbac            = true
  enable_telemetry       = var.enable_telemetry
  # CCC.K8S.CN17.AR01: kubelet identity distinct from the control-plane identity.
  identity_profile = {
    kubeletidentity = {
      resource_id = local.kubelet_identity_id
    }
  }
  ignore_body_changes = var.ignore_body_changes.containerservice_managed_clusters
  # CCC.K8S.CN09.AR01: a <major.minor> or null version lets the patch channel keep the
  # cluster inside the support lifecycle without idempotency drift.
  kubernetes_version = var.kubernetes_version
  # CCC.K8S.CN09.AR02: upgrades run inside weekly maintenance windows.
  maintenanceconfiguration = {
    aksManagedAutoUpgradeSchedule = {
      name = "aksManagedAutoUpgradeSchedule"
      maintenance_window = {
        duration_hours = 4
        start_time     = "00:00"
        utc_offset     = "+00:00"
        schedule = {
          weekly = {
            day_of_week    = "Sunday"
            interval_weeks = 1
          }
        }
      }
    }
    aksManagedNodeOSUpgradeSchedule = {
      name = "aksManagedNodeOSUpgradeSchedule"
      maintenance_window = {
        duration_hours = 4
        start_time     = "00:00"
        utc_offset     = "+00:00"
        schedule = {
          weekly = {
            day_of_week    = "Saturday"
            interval_weeks = 1
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
  # CCC.K8S.CN17.AR01: dedicated control-plane identity.
  managed_identities = {
    system_assigned            = false
    user_assigned_resource_ids = [local.control_plane_identity_id]
  }
  # CCC.K8S.CN06.AR01, CN12.AR03, CN13.AR02, CN15.AR01: managed namespaces with
  # default-deny network policy (which also blocks IMDS), quotas and ownership metadata.
  namespace = {
    for key, ns in var.workload_namespaces : key => {
      name = key
      labels = merge(ns.labels, {
        "data-classification" = ns.data_classification
      })
      annotations = {
        "ccc.finos.org/owner" = ns.owner
      }
      default_network_policy = {
        ingress = "DenyAll"
        egress  = "DenyAll"
      }
      default_resource_quota = ns.resource_quota
      adoption_policy        = "Never"
      delete_policy          = "Delete"
      tags                   = var.tags
    }
  }
  # CCC.K8S.CN06: Cilium enforces the namespace network policies.
  network_profile = {
    load_balancer_sku   = "standard"
    outbound_type       = var.outbound_type
    network_plugin      = "azure"
    network_plugin_mode = "overlay"
    network_dataplane   = "cilium"
    network_policy      = "cilium"
    pod_cidr            = "172.18.0.0/16"
    service_cidr        = var.service_cidr
    dns_service_ip      = var.dns_service_ip
  }
  # CCC.K8S.CN15.AR02: block out-of-band changes to the AKS-managed node resource group.
  node_resource_group_profile = {
    restriction_level = "ReadOnly"
  }
  # CCC.K8S.CN03.AR01: OIDC issuer for federated workload identities.
  oidc_issuer_profile = {
    enabled = local.enabled_cluster_features.workload_identity
  }
  # CCC.K8S.CN01.AR02: public network access to the API server is disabled.
  public_network_access = "Disabled"
  resource_types        = var.resource_types.containerservice_managed_clusters
  retry                 = var.retry
  # CCC.K8S.CN02.AR01: scoped Azure RBAC for Kubernetes role assignments.
  role_assignments = local.cluster_role_assignments
  # CCC.K8S.CN03.AR01: workload identity. CCC.K8S.CN07.AR01: private Key Vault KMS for
  # Kubernetes secrets. CCC.K8S.CN14.AR01 / CCC.Core.CN07: Defender threat detection.
  security_profile = {
    workload_identity = {
      enabled = local.enabled_cluster_features.workload_identity
    }
    azure_key_vault_kms = {
      enabled                  = local.enabled_cluster_features.azure_key_vault_kms
      key_id                   = local.key_vault_key_id
      key_vault_network_access = "Private"
      key_vault_resource_id    = local.key_vault_resource_id
    }
    defender = {
      log_analytics_workspace_resource_id = module.log_analytics.resource_id
      security_monitoring = {
        enabled = local.enabled_cluster_features.defender
      }
    }
    image_cleaner = {
      enabled        = local.enabled_cluster_features.image_cleaner
      interval_hours = 48
    }
  }
  # CCC.K8S.CN09: Standard tier with an uptime SLA.
  sku = {
    name = "Base"
    tier = "Standard"
  }
  # CCC.K8S.CN15.AR01: approved ownership, environment and data-classification tags.
  tags     = var.tags
  timeouts = var.timeouts

  depends_on = [
    time_sleep.rbac_propagation,
    module.api_dns_zone,
  ]
}

check "approved_addons_only" {
  assert {
    condition     = length(setsubtract(local.enabled_addons, var.approved_addons)) == 0
    error_message = "Every enabled AKS add-on must be in var.approved_addons (CCC.K8S.CN08.AR01)."
  }
}
```

## Required Inputs

No required inputs.

## Optional Inputs

The following input variables are optional (have default values):

### <a name="input_api_server_subnet_id"></a> [api\_server\_subnet\_id](#input\_api\_server\_subnet\_id)

Description: Existing API-server subnet ARM ID delegated to Microsoft.ContainerService/managedClusters (/28 or larger) in the node subnet's VNet, or null when the network is created.

Type: `string`

Default: `null`

### <a name="input_approved_addons"></a> [approved\_addons](#input\_approved\_addons)

Description: Organization-approved allowlist of AKS add-ons and managed security features (CCC.K8S.CN08.AR01). A check fails when the example enables anything else.

Type: `list(string)`

Default:

```json
[
  "azure_key_vault_kms",
  "azure_policy",
  "defender",
  "image_cleaner",
  "oms_agent",
  "workload_identity"
]
```

### <a name="input_cluster_admin_group_object_ids"></a> [cluster\_admin\_group\_object\_ids](#input\_cluster\_admin\_group\_object\_ids)

Description: Optional break-glass Entra GROUP object IDs that receive Kubernetes cluster-admin through the AAD profile. Day-to-day access uses `cluster_role_assignments`.

Type: `list(string)`

Default: `[]`

### <a name="input_cluster_role_assignments"></a> [cluster\_role\_assignments](#input\_cluster\_role\_assignments)

Description: Azure RBAC for Kubernetes role assignments at cluster scope (CCC.K8S.CN02.AR01). Prefer groups  
and the narrowest built-in role, for example `Azure Kubernetes Service RBAC Reader` or
`Azure Kubernetes Service RBAC Writer`. When empty, the deploying identity receives
`Azure Kubernetes Service RBAC Cluster Admin` so the example remains operable.

- `principal_id` - Entra object ID of the user, group or service principal.
- `role_definition_id_or_name` - Built-in role name or role definition ID.
- `principal_type` - Optional `User`, `Group` or `ServicePrincipal`.

Type:

```hcl
map(object({
    principal_id               = string
    role_definition_id_or_name = string
    principal_type             = optional(string)
  }))
```

Default: `{}`

### <a name="input_container_cpu_limit"></a> [container\_cpu\_limit](#input\_container\_cpu\_limit)

Description: Maximum CPU limit allowed for any user container by Azure Policy (CCC.K8S.CN13.AR01).

Type: `string`

Default: `"1000m"`

### <a name="input_container_memory_limit"></a> [container\_memory\_limit](#input\_container\_memory\_limit)

Description: Maximum memory limit allowed for any user container by Azure Policy (CCC.K8S.CN13.AR01).

Type: `string`

Default: `"2Gi"`

### <a name="input_container_registry_private_dns_zone_id"></a> [container\_registry\_private\_dns\_zone\_id](#input\_container\_registry\_private\_dns\_zone\_id)

Description: Existing privatelink.azurecr.io DNS zone ARM ID already resolvable from the cluster VNet, or null to create the zone and link it to the cluster VNet.

Type: `string`

Default: `null`

### <a name="input_container_registry_private_endpoint_subnet_id"></a> [container\_registry\_private\_endpoint\_subnet\_id](#input\_container\_registry\_private\_endpoint\_subnet\_id)

Description: Existing subnet ARM ID, reachable from the AKS nodes, for the container registry private endpoint, or null when the network is created.

Type: `string`

Default: `null`

### <a name="input_control_plane_identity_id"></a> [control\_plane\_identity\_id](#input\_control\_plane\_identity\_id)

Description: Existing control-plane user-assigned identity ARM ID, or null to create one. Existing-to-existing grants remain the caller's responsibility.

Type: `string`

Default: `null`

### <a name="input_disk_encryption_set_id"></a> [disk\_encryption\_set\_id](#input\_disk\_encryption\_set\_id)

Description: Existing disk encryption set ARM ID with usable CMK/grants, or null to create a system-assigned DES and a separate disk key in the selected vault. Existing DES keys and grants are not managed.

Type: `string`

Default: `null`

### <a name="input_dns_service_ip"></a> [dns\_service\_ip](#input\_dns\_service\_ip)

Description: Kubernetes DNS service IP within service\_cidr.

Type: `string`

Default: `"10.20.0.10"`

### <a name="input_enable_telemetry"></a> [enable\_telemetry](#input\_enable\_telemetry)

Description: This variable controls whether or not telemetry is enabled for the module.  
For more information see <https://aka.ms/avm/telemetryinfo>.  
If it is set to false, then no telemetry will be collected.

Type: `bool`

Default: `true`

### <a name="input_ignore_body_changes"></a> [ignore\_body\_changes](#input\_ignore\_body\_changes)

Description: Body-relative ignore paths passed to AKS unchanged. Only tags may be ignored; ignored configuration is not sent to Azure until the path is removed and changes take effect only after apply. Published prerequisite AVMs own their lifecycle interfaces.

Type:

```hcl
object({
    containerservice_managed_clusters = optional(object({
      containerservice_managed_clusters = optional(list(string), [])
    }), {})
  })
```

Default: `{}`

### <a name="input_key_vault_dns_virtual_network_links"></a> [key\_vault\_dns\_virtual\_network\_links](#input\_key\_vault\_dns\_virtual\_network\_links)

Description: Map of NEW DNS link names to existing VNet ARM IDs for vault resolution (runner VNet or DNS-forwarding hub). When the network is created, the created runner VNet is linked automatically. Do not link the cluster VNet: AKS private KMS links its own zone there. Existing links are never adopted.

Type: `map(string)`

Default: `{}`

### <a name="input_key_vault_key_id"></a> [key\_vault\_key\_id](#input\_key\_vault\_key\_id)

Description: Existing versioned KMS key HTTPS URL, paired with key\_vault\_resource\_id, or null to create a separate RSA KMS key in the selected vault. This is a data-plane URL, not an ARM key ID.

Type: `string`

Default: `null`

### <a name="input_key_vault_private_dns_zone_id"></a> [key\_vault\_private\_dns\_zone\_id](#input\_key\_vault\_private\_dns\_zone\_id)

Description: Existing privatelink.vaultcore.azure.net DNS zone ARM ID, or null to create it through AVM when keys are created. Existing zones are not imported. For full key/DES reuse no vault endpoint or DNS resources are created.

Type: `string`

Default: `null`

### <a name="input_key_vault_private_endpoint_subnet_id"></a> [key\_vault\_private\_endpoint\_subnet\_id](#input\_key\_vault\_private\_endpoint\_subnet\_id)

Description: Existing non-delegated subnet ARM ID for the deployment runner's Key Vault private endpoint, or null when the network is created (the endpoint then goes into the created runner VNet). Runner routing, NSGs and TCP 443 access must work.

Type: `string`

Default: `null`

### <a name="input_key_vault_resource_id"></a> [key\_vault\_resource\_id](#input\_key\_vault\_resource\_id)

Description: Existing KMS vault ARM ID, or null to create a private, RBAC-enabled, purge-protected vault. Creating keys or new identity grants in an existing vault requires RBAC mode; creating a DES also requires purge protection and the cluster region.

Type: `string`

Default: `null`

### <a name="input_kubelet_identity_id"></a> [kubelet\_identity\_id](#input\_kubelet\_identity\_id)

Description: Existing kubelet user-assigned identity ARM ID (not an object/client ID), or null to create one distinct from the control-plane identity.

Type: `string`

Default: `null`

### <a name="input_kubernetes_version"></a> [kubernetes\_version](#input\_kubernetes\_version)

Description: Kubernetes `<major.minor>` version supported in the selected region, or null for the AKS default. The patch upgrade channel keeps the patch level current (CCC.K8S.CN09).

Type: `string`

Default: `null`

### <a name="input_location"></a> [location](#input\_location)

Description: Approved Azure region (CCC.Core.CN06). It must support availability zones 1-3, Trusted Launch, encryption at host and the Standard\_D4s\_v5 VM size.

Type: `string`

Default: `"swedencentral"`

### <a name="input_log_analytics_retention_in_days"></a> [log\_analytics\_retention\_in\_days](#input\_log\_analytics\_retention\_in\_days)

Description: Retention for Kubernetes audit, control-plane and security logs in the Log Analytics workspace (CCC.K8S.CN14.AR01).

Type: `number`

Default: `90`

### <a name="input_name"></a> [name](#input\_name)

Description: Optional new cluster name. When null, a unique aks-ccc name is generated and retained in state. Never target an existing cluster with new state.

Type: `string`

Default: `null`

### <a name="input_outbound_type"></a> [outbound\_type](#input\_outbound\_type)

Description: AKS outbound type. `userDefinedRouting` requires existing subnets whose route table already sends egress through an approved firewall.

Type: `string`

Default: `"loadBalancer"`

### <a name="input_private_dns_zone_id"></a> [private\_dns\_zone\_id](#input\_private\_dns\_zone\_id)

Description: Existing API private DNS zone ARM ID, including a cross-subscription zone, or null to create a unique subzone of private.<location>.azmk8s.io linked to the cluster VNet. Existing zone links are not managed.

Type: `string`

Default: `null`

### <a name="input_resource_group_id"></a> [resource\_group\_id](#input\_resource\_group\_id)

Description: Existing resource group ARM ID for the cluster and its prerequisites, or null to create one.

Type: `string`

Default: `null`

### <a name="input_resource_types"></a> [resource\_types](#input\_resource\_types)

Description: API versions for read-only prerequisite lookups and the AKS module. Published prerequisite AVMs own their resource API versions.

- `compute_disk_encryption_sets` - Read the new DES principal ID.
- `keyvault_vaults` - Validate an existing vault without adopting it.
- `managedidentity_user_assigned_identities` - Read an existing control-plane principal ID.
- `containerservice_managed_clusters` - Overrides passed to AKS unchanged.
- `containerservice_managed_clusters.containerservice_managed_clusters` - AKS cluster API version.
- `containerservice_managed_clusters.containerservice_managed_clusters_agent_pools` - Default agent pool API version.

Type:

```hcl
object({
    compute_disk_encryption_sets             = optional(string, "Microsoft.Compute/diskEncryptionSets@2024-03-02")
    keyvault_vaults                          = optional(string, "Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults@2024-11-01")
    managedidentity_user_assigned_identities = optional(string, "Microsoft.ManagedIdentity/userAssignedIdentities@2024-11-30")
    containerservice_managed_clusters = optional(object({
      containerservice_managed_clusters             = optional(string)
      containerservice_managed_clusters_agent_pools = optional(string)
    }), {})
  })
```

Default: `{}`

### <a name="input_retry"></a> [retry](#input\_retry)

Description: AKS retry configuration. The default retries transient authorization errors while new role assignments propagate. Null uses provider defaults. Published prerequisite AVMs own their retry behavior; this input does not configure them.

Type:

```hcl
object({
    error_message_regex  = optional(list(string))
    interval_seconds     = optional(number)
    max_interval_seconds = optional(number)
  })
```

Default:

```json
{
  "error_message_regex": [
    "AuthorizationFailed",
    "LinkedAuthorizationFailed",
    "MissingPermission",
    "PrincipalNotFound"
  ],
  "interval_seconds": 30,
  "max_interval_seconds": 120
}
```

### <a name="input_runner_virtual_network_address_space"></a> [runner\_virtual\_network\_address\_space](#input\_runner\_virtual\_network\_address\_space)

Description: Address space of the created runner VNet (/26 or larger), which hosts the deployment runner and its Key Vault private endpoint.

Type: `string`

Default: `"10.11.0.0/24"`

### <a name="input_service_cidr"></a> [service\_cidr](#input\_service\_cidr)

Description: Kubernetes service CIDR. It must not overlap the VNets, connected networks or the fixed pod CIDR 172.18.0.0/16.

Type: `string`

Default: `"10.20.0.0/16"`

### <a name="input_subnet_id"></a> [subnet\_id](#input\_subnet\_id)

Description: Existing AKS node subnet ARM ID, or null to create the cluster and runner VNets. Supply all existing subnet inputs together or none of them.

Type: `string`

Default: `null`

### <a name="input_subscription_id"></a> [subscription\_id](#input\_subscription\_id)

Description: Subscription ID used when `resource_group_id` is null. When both are null, AzAPI uses the Azure CLI default subscription and AzureRM requires `ARM_SUBSCRIPTION_ID`.

Type: `string`

Default: `null`

### <a name="input_tags"></a> [tags](#input\_tags)

Description: Approved ownership, environment and data-classification tags applied to resources that support tags (CCC.K8S.CN15.AR01).

Type: `map(string)`

Default:

```json
{
  "data-classification": "internal",
  "environment": "demo",
  "owner": "platform-team"
}
```

### <a name="input_timeouts"></a> [timeouts](#input\_timeouts)

Description: Optional AKS operation timeouts, such as 30m or 1h. Null uses provider defaults. Published prerequisite AVMs own their timeout behavior; this input does not configure them.

Type:

```hcl
object({
    create = optional(string)
    read   = optional(string)
    update = optional(string)
    delete = optional(string)
  })
```

Default: `null`

### <a name="input_virtual_network_address_space"></a> [virtual\_network\_address\_space](#input\_virtual\_network\_address\_space)

Description: Address space of the created cluster VNet (/16 or larger). Nodes, the API server and private endpoints receive fixed subnets inside it.

Type: `string`

Default: `"10.10.0.0/16"`

### <a name="input_workload_namespaces"></a> [workload\_namespaces](#input\_workload\_namespaces)

Description: User workload namespaces created as AKS managed namespaces. Each namespace denies all ingress  
and egress by default (CCC.K8S.CN06.AR01), has a resource quota (CCC.K8S.CN13.AR02), carries  
ownership metadata (CCC.K8S.CN15.AR01) and gets a dedicated federated workload identity for  
the named service account (CCC.K8S.CN03.AR01). The map key is the namespace name.

- `owner` - Owning team, recorded as an annotation.
- `data_classification` - Data classification, recorded as a label.
- `service_account_name` - Kubernetes service account federated to the workload identity.
- `labels` - Additional namespace labels.
- `resource_quota` - Aggregate CPU and memory requests and limits for the namespace.

Type:

```hcl
map(object({
    owner                = string
    data_classification  = string
    service_account_name = optional(string, "workload")
    labels               = optional(map(string), {})
    resource_quota = optional(object({
      cpu_limit      = optional(string, "2000m")
      cpu_request    = optional(string, "1000m")
      memory_limit   = optional(string, "4Gi")
      memory_request = optional(string, "2Gi")
    }), {})
  }))
```

Default:

```json
{
  "workload-a": {
    "data_classification": "internal",
    "owner": "platform-team"
  }
}
```

## Outputs

The following outputs are exported:

### <a name="output_cluster_id"></a> [cluster\_id](#output\_cluster\_id)

Description: ARM resource ID of the new AKS cluster.

### <a name="output_cluster_name"></a> [cluster\_name](#output\_cluster\_name)

Description: Name of the new AKS cluster, including its generated suffix when no name is supplied.

### <a name="output_container_registry_login_server"></a> [container\_registry\_login\_server](#output\_container\_registry\_login\_server)

Description: Login server of the approved private container registry. Admitted images must use this registry and an @sha256 digest.

### <a name="output_control_plane_identity_id"></a> [control\_plane\_identity\_id](#output\_control\_plane\_identity\_id)

Description: ARM ID of the created or reused control-plane identity.

### <a name="output_disk_encryption_set_id"></a> [disk\_encryption\_set\_id](#output\_disk\_encryption\_set\_id)

Description: ARM ID of the created or reused node disk encryption set.

### <a name="output_disk_key_id"></a> [disk\_key\_id](#output\_disk\_key\_id)

Description: Versioned disk-key URL when a DES is created; null when reusing a DES, whose key remains externally managed.

### <a name="output_key_vault_key_id"></a> [key\_vault\_key\_id](#output\_key\_vault\_key\_id)

Description: Versioned HTTPS URL of the created or reused KMS key.

### <a name="output_key_vault_private_dns_zone_id"></a> [key\_vault\_private\_dns\_zone\_id](#output\_key\_vault\_private\_dns\_zone\_id)

Description: Selected vault private DNS zone ARM ID; null for full key/DES reuse with an explicit null DNS input.

### <a name="output_key_vault_private_endpoint_id"></a> [key\_vault\_private\_endpoint\_id](#output\_key\_vault\_private\_endpoint\_id)

Description: Runner vault private endpoint ARM ID, or null when no keys are managed by this example.

### <a name="output_key_vault_resource_id"></a> [key\_vault\_resource\_id](#output\_key\_vault\_resource\_id)

Description: ARM ID of the created or reused KMS vault.

### <a name="output_kubelet_identity_id"></a> [kubelet\_identity\_id](#output\_kubelet\_identity\_id)

Description: ARM ID of the distinct created or reused kubelet identity.

### <a name="output_log_analytics_workspace_id"></a> [log\_analytics\_workspace\_id](#output\_log\_analytics\_workspace\_id)

Description: ARM ID of the Log Analytics workspace receiving Kubernetes audit, control-plane and Defender data.

### <a name="output_oidc_issuer_url"></a> [oidc\_issuer\_url](#output\_oidc\_issuer\_url)

Description: OIDC issuer URL used by the workload identity federated credentials.

### <a name="output_private_dns_zone_id"></a> [private\_dns\_zone\_id](#output\_private\_dns\_zone\_id)

Description: ARM ID of the created or reused API-server private DNS zone.

### <a name="output_private_fqdn"></a> [private\_fqdn](#output\_private\_fqdn)

Description: Private API-server FQDN; access requires connectivity and DNS resolution through the approved private network.

### <a name="output_resource_group_id"></a> [resource\_group\_id](#output\_resource\_group\_id)

Description: ARM ID of the created or reused resource group.

### <a name="output_runner_subnet_id"></a> [runner\_subnet\_id](#output\_runner\_subnet\_id)

Description: Subnet for a self-hosted runner or jump host that can reach the Key Vault private endpoint; null when existing subnets are supplied.

### <a name="output_workload_identity_client_ids"></a> [workload\_identity\_client\_ids](#output\_workload\_identity\_client\_ids)

Description: Client ID of each namespace's workload identity, for the `azure.workload.identity/client-id` service account annotation.

You may turn off the telemetry as described in the repository. There are also some features in the software that may enable you and Microsoft to collect data from users of your applications. If you use these features, you must comply with applicable law, including providing appropriate notices to users of your applications together with a copy of Microsoft’s privacy statement. Our privacy statement is located at <https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkID=824704>. You can learn more about data collection and use in the help documentation and our privacy statement. Your use of the software operates as your consent to these practices.
